name: Priya Diaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and your answers stay confidential. What is a normal day at the accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional accountancy qualification, preparing accounts and tax returns for community transport clients. I like finding the driver sheet that explains a missing bank deposit, but I get tired of ringing three offices for the same ticket book. Salim and I have grown children and about four months of costs saved, so retirement is in sight without any promise that the mortgage is covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small software saving would not change the pile of bus-service invoices on my desk. I still need the driver sheet when the ticket total and the bank deposit differ.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to keep a person on every subsidy correction. A community route can lose its funding over a number nobody has explained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used an AI tool at work; I need to see a check succeed before I trust a new screen. My pay is typical for an accountant and Salim and I have four months saved, so the ordinary week is manageable but not carefree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned accounts and returns for the transport clients, matching ticket logs to bank lines. I would bring the missing Tuesday deposit to senior reviewer Mara at the next paid file review.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy because four months is useful but there is still a mortgage and no confirmed later income. Some similar accounting firms are nearby, though a move is not in my plan today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened with the Tuesday bus?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The Tuesday bus had a paper ticket book that never reached the office, and the bank deposit looked too small. I liked finding the driver’s envelope; I did not enjoy making three calls for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks your final tax treatment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mara checks my final tax treatment, even after years in this work. My professional qualification taught me the rules, but a real ticket book still has to turn up.

say: I would keep a **human explanation** for every subsidy correction.
I would ask for the **driver sheet** before changing a ticket total.
think: I have **never used AI** with client accounts.
Four months saved helps, but the **mortgage** still needs wages.
do: Keep preparing **assigned bus accounts** and matching ticket logs against bank deposits.
Bring the **missing Tuesday deposit** to Mara’s next paid review.
feel: **Uneasy** about the mortgage and later income despite steady current work.
S0.quote: The Tuesday bus had a paper ticket book that never reached the office, and the bank deposit looked too small.
fieldNote: Her **Tuesday bus** example grounds careful paper checks and shows why she values explanation over a tidy software total.
Typical pay, **four months saved** and some nearby firms support an uneasy baseline without assuming pension income.

steps.text: Keep assigned bus accounts checked against ticket logs and bank deposits
Bring missing Tuesday deposit to Mara at next paid review

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes and checks the bus accounts, I expect fewer people will be paid to chase missing ticket books. The later robots do not delay what happens to these screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask our union for written paid checking hours and a way for passengers to challenge a wrong subsidy record. I would tell colleagues not to sign a return they cannot explain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own paid hours could shrink even though I know these routes. Four months saved buys some search time, but Salim’s library wage would not replace my usual pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid discrepancy files Mara assigns and ask her for two paid supervised sessions learning the passenger appeal letters; if approved, I will handle two real cases. If refused, I will study free published letters while keeping only paid accounts still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own income, but I can make a careful request before the hours change. I would not upload a passenger list into an unapproved tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would you search after an hours cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my paid hours actually fall, I will apply for posted rent-accounts work at the housing office. I would leave only with written pay covering our mortgage and food, confirmed start and hours fitting Salim’s shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the appeal training involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A passenger appeal starts with the ticket log and the fare decision, then a letter that a person can read. Mara would check my answer before it went out, and the time must be paid.

say: I would ask our **union** for paid checking hours and passenger appeal rights.
I would tell colleagues to **explain returns** before signing them.
think: My own **paid hours** could shrink even with route knowledge.
Four months saved cannot replace my wage beside the **mortgage**.
do: Learn **two paid supervised appeals** only if Mara assigns them; otherwise study free letters while paid files last.
If hours fall, seek **posted housing accounts** with written pay covering mortgage and food, confirmed start and Salim-compatible hours.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible loss of my own hours.
S1.quote: A passenger appeal starts with the ticket log and the fare decision, then a letter that a person can read.
fieldNote: The **appeal practice** requires two assigned real cases, paid time and Mara’s supervision, with free letters as fallback.
A **housing-office move** starts after actual hours fall and requires an advertised vacancy plus written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Ask union for written paid checking hours and passenger appeal rights
Handle two passenger appeals only if Mara assigns supervised paid cases
Otherwise study free letters while assigned paid bus accounts remain
If hours fall, seek posted housing-accounts: written pay covering mortgage and food, confirmed start, Salim-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could do our accounts thinking before hands-on robots reach buses around 2031. The ticket counter still has scheduling and fare records that change in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union for dated pay notices and tell riders to keep their ticket evidence. I would not tell them a new protection rule has already been passed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect our firm to cut most paid bus-account review in the first year after 2028, including my hours. Four months saved and Salim’s wage give us some breathing room, but the mortgage would keep coming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would postpone our planned garden work and keep its monthly payment in the bill account now. After 2028, if my paid bus-account hours are cut, I would seek posted housing-office rent-records work only with written pay covering mortgage and food, confirmed start and workable hours; I would take paid firm bus-account cases only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about a likely large income loss, even with four months saved. I can search, but the housing office may not have a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which expense can wait?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The garden fence can wait one season, and my partner Salim agrees the existing gate still closes. I would not claim new savings until the planned payment actually remains in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would rent records escape AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The housing office has desk records that AGI could handle too. I would see a posted paid role as a chance to earn, not a permanent refuge from software.

say: I would ask for **dated pay notices** through the union.
I would say **rent records** face AGI just like bus accounts.
think: I expect a **large cut** in my paid hours after 2028.
Four months saved cannot carry the **mortgage** indefinitely.
do: Postpone the **garden fence** and retain its planned payment; keep paid bus-account cases only while offered.
After 2028 paid-hour cuts, seek **posted housing records** with written pay covering mortgage and food, confirmed start and workable hours.
Ask the **union** for dated pay notices before bus-account hours end.
S2.quote: The garden fence can wait one season, and my partner Salim agrees the existing gate still closes.
fieldNote: The **deferred fence** retains current cash for mortgage bills rather than relabelling old savings as new money.
Her **housing-office option** also faces desk AGI; a posted vacancy and written wage are necessary, not proof of safety.

steps.text: Postpone garden fence and retain planned payment for bills
Take paid firm bus-account cases only while offered
After 2028 cuts, seek posted housing: written pay covering mortgage and food, confirmed start, workable hours
Ask union for dated pay notices before bus-account hours end

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years before 2031 gives us time to find out which passenger disputes still pay for a person. The bus accounts desk still changes in 2031, before 2034 robots matter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union for an annual count of paid appeal cases and a fair rota. I would not want the same two people to absorb all the unpaid client calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep paid appeal work, but I cannot assume the firm will sell enough of it after AGI. At 63 I still need the mortgage paid from actual income, not an imagined retirement figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Mara for one assigned paid supervised fare appeal each quarter and complete it if the firm agrees. If refused, I will use free published case letters for practice while continuing paid bus returns only while offered, including in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the wage but I can use five years to learn the appeal rules. I would not fund a course from our four month reserve without a real paid place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would one real appeal require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One case would mean checking the rider’s ticket, the route timetable and the refusal letter, then drafting a reply for Mara to review. I want to know which hour the firm will actually pay for. One rider’s appeal can take an hour the firm does not pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if paid appeals disappear?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If paid appeals disappear after 2031 and we still need my wage, I will apply for posted housing rent-accounts work only with written pay covering our mortgage, confirmed start and hours compatible with Salim’s shifts. I would keep current paid files only while offered.

say: I would seek a **fair paid-appeal rota** through the union.
I would date bus-account risk to **2031**, before robots.
think: I cannot assume **paid appeal demand** survives AGI.
Our mortgage needs **actual income** at 63, not guessed retirement money.
do: Complete **quarterly paid appeal** only if the firm assigns Mara’s supervision; otherwise study free letters while paid returns last.
After 2031 appeal loss, seek **posted rent accounts** only if wage needed, with written mortgage-covering pay, confirmed start and Salim-compatible shifts.
Ask the **union yearly** for paid appeal counts and a fair rota.
S3.quote: One rider’s appeal can take an hour the firm does not pay.
fieldNote: The **quarterly appeal** is paid case practice with Mara, contingent on firm assignment rather than a training request alone.
Free letters and **current paid bus returns** remain the fallback only while files are offered.

steps.text: Ask union for annual paid-appeal counts and fair rota
Complete quarterly supervised fare appeal only if firm assigns Mara and paid time
Otherwise practise free letters while assigned paid bus returns remain after 2031
After paid-appeal loss, seek posted housing if wage needed: written mortgage-covering pay, confirmed start, Salim-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 makes me 68, and I hope to have time away from a desk. Full AGI still reaches the bus accounts in 2036 before physical robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union for yearly paid-hour figures and tell younger colleagues to keep the rider’s evidence. I would not say my age makes their problem smaller.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know if Salim and I will have enough confirmed income to stop working in 2036. Four months saved is helpful but it is not a retirement plan for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns and transfer twenty-five from each monthly wage into a repair reserve if the mortgage and food bills allow. After 2036, only if actual income still leaves a mortgage gap and the firm cuts my hours, I would seek posted housing-office accounts work with written pay covering that gap, confirmed start and workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now because ten years gives us time to measure the problem. I would be anxious if paid work stopped before the bills were covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if household costs rise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The twenty-five is from today’s wages, not our four months already saved. I would stop it if Salim’s library hours fell or the mortgage rate rose.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would grown children help with the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children can come for supper, but I would not expect them to take over our mortgage. I will decide about stopping work from real income and bills, not a birthday.

say: I would ask for **yearly paid-hour figures** through the union.
I would tell younger colleagues to retain **rider evidence**.
think: I cannot count **unconfirmed later income** against the mortgage.
Four months saved gives time, not a **retirement wage**.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** while offered and save twenty-five monthly from wages if mortgage and food allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted housing accounts** only if mortgage gap remains, with written gap-covering pay, start and hours.
Ask the **union yearly** for paid-hour figures before planning fewer workdays.
feel: **Uneasy** now; anxious if paid work ends first.
S4.quote: Our grown children can come for supper, but I would not expect them to take over our mortgage.
fieldNote: Her **repair reserve** grows from new wages and stops if Salim’s hours fall or the mortgage rate rises.
Any **post-2036 move** needs a verified gap, actual reduced paid hours, posted work and written terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid bus returns only while offered
Save twenty-five from wages if bills allow; pause if Salim loses hours or mortgage rises
After 2036 cuts, seek posted housing only if gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/hours
Ask union yearly for paid bus-account hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the paid bus-account work could shrink before another wage starts. Dated pay notices, a fair paid-appeal rota and a posted job with written wages would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who sits behind a subsidy number. A missing Tuesday ticket book can decide whether a community bus runs next month.

headlineQuote: A missing Tuesday ticket book can decide whether a community bus runs next month.
portrait: Priya is a **58 year old experienced** accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who prepares community-transport accounts.
She has **never used AI**, relying on ticket logs and driver sheets to explain bank deposits and subsidies.
Typical pay, Salim’s library wage, grown children, **four months saved** and some nearby firms make the plateau uneasy.
She asks the **union** for paid appeals and requires actual posted written terms before any housing-office move.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could cut her paid bus accounts before a new wage begins.
whatWouldHelp: **Dated pay notices**, paid appeal work and a posted job with written wages would help.
